verdict.rationale: Pulumi documents its own testing modes that avoid production. Unit tests run in memory and mock all external calls, and integration tests deploy ephemeral infrastructure to test against, which is sandbox-style isolation rather than a mere dry-run. `pulumi preview` makes no changes, but it is a dry-run rather than a sandbox, so it is not credited as one. The docs do not explicitly say the ephemeral environments are kept separate from production data. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of production-data isolation for test environments, detail on provisioning and tearing down sandbox stacks, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Integration Tests deploy ephemeral infrastructure and run external tests against it.
Unit Tests are fast in-memory tests that mock all external calls.
Because Pulumi uses general purpose programming languages to provision cloud resources, you can take advantage of native testing frameworks
